misconceptions.error: Thinks being special means being better than other people.

example.question: What does it mean that you are God's special creation?
example.wrong_answer: You are better than other children
example.correct_answer: God made you with love and no one else is exactly like you

misconceptions.cause: The word special is heard as a prize or a rank.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "You are better than other children" beside "God made you with love and no one else is exactly like you" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say that every child is special in the same way, and ask each child to name one thing that makes a classmate special.
misconceptions.feedback: Everyone is God's special creation. Being special does not make you better than others, because God made them with love too.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a person is a chance event, without a plan or a maker.

example.question: According to Psalm 139:13-14, how did God make you?
example.correct_answer: He knit you together, fearfully and wonderfully made

misconceptions.cause: Science lessons and talk about birth leave out God as the maker.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "By chance, with no plan" beside "He knit you together, fearfully and wonderfully made" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Psalm 139:13-14 slowly and ask who is doing the knitting.
misconceptions.feedback: Psalm 139:13-14 says that God formed each person and that we are fearfully and wonderfully made. You were not made by chance.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks God made only the first people, Adam and Eve, not each person today.

example.question: Who made you, according to the Bible?
example.wrong_answer: God made only the first man and woman, and I came from my parents only
example.correct_answer: God, who made every person in his image

misconceptions.cause: The creation story is told as a story of long ago only.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "God made only the first man and woman, and I came from my parents only" beside "God, who made every person in his image" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Link Genesis 1:27 ("God created mankind in his own image") to Psalm 139:13 about each person.
misconceptions.feedback: Genesis 1:27 says God made human beings in his image, and Psalm 139:13 says he formed each of us. God is the maker of every person, including you.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks that feeling angry is itself a sin.

example.question: What does Ephesians 4:26 say about anger?
example.correct_answer: Do not sin when you are angry

misconceptions.cause: The child hears only the warning about anger.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Never feel angry at all" beside "Do not sin when you are angry" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read the verse: it says "in your anger do not sin". Ask what the angry child can do instead of hitting or shouting.
misconceptions.feedback: Ephesians 4:26 says "in your anger do not sin". Anger is a feeling that comes to everyone. The wrong is in what we do with it.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks you should keep anger inside until you can get even.

example.question: What should you do about anger, according to Ephesians 4:26?
example.wrong_answer: Keep it and pay the person back later
example.correct_answer: Settle it before the sun goes down

misconceptions.cause: Revenge looks like justice to a hurt child.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Keep it and pay the person back later" beside "Settle it before the sun goes down" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Role-play saying sorry or forgiving before bedtime.
misconceptions.feedback: Ephesians 4:26 says do not let the sun go down while you are still angry. Settle it quickly by forgiving or talking, not by planning to pay back.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks we rejoice only when everything is going well.

example.question: What does Philippians 4:4 tell us to do?
example.wrong_answer: Rejoice only when things go well
example.correct_answer: Rejoice in the Lord always

misconceptions.cause: Joy is mixed up with having what we want.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Rejoice only when things go well" beside "Rejoice in the Lord always" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask whether we can be thankful to God even on a hard day, and why.
misconceptions.feedback: Philippians 4:4 says "Rejoice in the Lord always". Our joy rests on God, who does not change, and not only on good days.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a choice has no result if nobody sees it.

example.question: Kamau takes a pencil that is not his and nobody sees. What is true?
example.wrong_answer: There is no result because nobody saw
example.correct_answer: It still has results: he did wrong and he knows it

misconceptions.cause: The child links wrong only to being caught.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "There is no result because nobody saw" beside "It still has results: he did wrong and he knows it" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List the results of one choice: for the child, for the owner, and before God.
misconceptions.feedback: Every choice has a result, even a secret one. Taking what is not yours is wrong whether or not anyone sees.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the right choice is whatever friends are choosing.

example.question: Your friends tell you to skip class. How do you choose what to do?
example.correct_answer: Choose what pleases God, even if my friends choose differently

misconceptions.cause: Wanting to belong is stronger than wanting to be right.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Do what my friends do" beside "Choose what pleases God, even if my friends choose differently" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Role-play a polite NO and walking to class.
misconceptions.feedback: A right choice is guided by the word of God, not by what the group does. Choose to obey and attend, even when friends choose differently.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks only big decisions are choices.

example.question: Which of these is a choice a child makes?
example.wrong_answer: Only deciding which school to attend
example.correct_answer: What to say, who to play with and whether to obey

misconceptions.cause: The child links choosing with grown-up decisions.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only deciding which school to attend" beside "What to say, who to play with and whether to obey" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Make a list of the choices in one school morning.
misconceptions.feedback: We make many choices every day: what to say, whom to sit with, whether to obey. Small choices matter too.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes the nuclear and the extended family.

example.question: Who belongs to the extended family?
example.correct_answer: Grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins

misconceptions.cause: The two names sound alike.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only mother, father and children" beside "Grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Draw a small circle for the home and a bigger circle around it for relatives.
misconceptions.feedback: The nuclear family is parents and their children. The extended family includes grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins too.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks family means only the people living in the same house.

example.question: Who counts as your family?
example.wrong_answer: Only those who live in my house
example.correct_answer: Those I live with and relatives who live elsewhere

misconceptions.cause: Many children see relatives rarely, and forget they are family.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only those who live in my house" beside "Those I live with and relatives who live elsewhere" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to name a relative who lives far away and how they keep in touch.
misconceptions.feedback: Your family includes relatives who do not live with you, such as a grandmother in the village. They are family even if you see them rarely.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks honouring parents is only for when they give us things or agree with us.

example.question: When should a child honour his parents, according to Ephesians 6:1-3?
example.wrong_answer: Only when they give me what I want
example.correct_answer: Always, because it is right

misconceptions.cause: Honour is mixed up with a bargain.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only when they give me what I want" beside "Always, because it is right" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Ephesians 6:1-3 and note the word "right" and the promise at the end.
misconceptions.feedback: Ephesians 6:1-3 says to obey and honour your parents because this is right, and that it brings a good life. Honour does not depend on gifts.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a child must keep a secret when an adult asks for it.

example.question: An adult touches you in a way that feels wrong and says "keep it a secret". What should you do?
example.wrong_answer: Keep the secret so I do not get in trouble
example.correct_answer: Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult

misconceptions.cause: The child fears trouble or is told to be quiet.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Keep the secret so I do not get in trouble" beside "Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say clearly: a secret about touching is never to be kept. Practise telling a teacher or parent.
misconceptions.feedback: A wrong touch is never a secret to keep. Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult, such as a parent or teacher, or call Childline Kenya on 116.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks only strangers can hurt a child and that people we know are always safe.

example.question: Who might touch a child in a wrong way?
example.correct_answer: Anyone, so a child must know what is not allowed and tell

misconceptions.cause: Warnings about strangers hide that harm can come from known people.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only strangers" beside "Anyone, so a child must know what is not allowed and tell" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Teach the rule: private parts are private, whoever asks.
misconceptions.feedback: Anyone can do wrong, even a person we know. The rule is that private parts are private. If anyone breaks it, say NO and tell a trusted adult.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks it is the child's fault if he or she is touched wrongly, so there is no need to tell.

example.question: A child was touched wrongly. Whose fault is it?
example.wrong_answer: The child's fault, so she should say nothing
example.correct_answer: Never the child's fault, and she should tell

misconceptions.cause: Shame and fear stop a child from telling.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The child's fault, so she should say nothing" beside "Never the child's fault, and she should tell" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say it slowly: it is never your fault. Name the adults who will believe and help.
misconceptions.feedback: It is never the child's fault. The person who touched wrongly did wrong. Tell a trusted adult, and keep telling until someone helps.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks God made the world together with others or that others made parts of it.

example.question: Who made everything, according to Genesis 1?
example.correct_answer: God alone

misconceptions.cause: Stories from other places mention many makers.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "God and other gods together" beside "God alone" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 1:1 and count how many makers are named.
misconceptions.feedback: Genesis 1 shows God as the sole creator. He alone made the heavens, the earth and everything in them.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks God loves only children who are good.

example.question: What does 1 John 4:7-8 say about God?
example.wrong_answer: God loves only the children who are always good
example.correct_answer: God is love

misconceptions.cause: A child learns that bad behaviour is punished and thinks love is the same.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "God loves only the children who are always good" beside "God is love" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read "God is love" and ask whether love is a reward.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 John 4:8 says "God is love". He is a loving Father to every child, and his love does not depend on being good all the time.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks holy means big, old or far away.

example.question: What does holy mean when we say God is holy?
example.correct_answer: Perfect and set apart, without sin

misconceptions.cause: The word is not used in daily speech.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Very big and old" beside "Perfect and set apart, without sin" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Link it to 1 Samuel 2:2: there is no one holy like the Lord.
misconceptions.feedback: Holy means set apart and perfect, without any sin. 1 Samuel 2:2 says there is no one holy like the Lord.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

skills.name: Know the story of Balaam and his donkey (Numbers 22) and why we obey God
skills.mastery: Says that Balak king of Moab sent for Balaam, that God told him to say only what God told him, that the donkey saw the angel of the Lord with a drawn sword three times before Balaam did, that the Lord opened the donkey's mouth and then Balaam's eyes, and that the lesson is to obey God. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Balaam saw the angel first.

example.question: Who saw the angel of the Lord first?
example.correct_answer: The donkey

misconceptions.cause: The child expects the prophet to see more than an animal.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Balaam" beside "The donkey" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Numbers 22:23 and 22:31 side by side.
misconceptions.feedback: The donkey saw the angel with the drawn sword first. Balaam saw him only when the Lord opened his eyes (Numbers 22:31).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks God allowed Balaam to curse the Israelites.

example.question: What was Balaam told to do about the Israelites?
example.correct_answer: Say only what God told him, and not curse them

misconceptions.cause: The child follows the king's offer and forgets God's word.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Curse them, for money" beside "Say only what God told him, and not curse them" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Numbers 22:12 and 22:20 aloud.
misconceptions.feedback: God told Balaam not to curse the people, and to do only what he was told (Numbers 22:12, 20). Speak well of others, not ill.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the donkey was stubborn and deserved to be beaten.

example.question: Why did the donkey turn aside and lie down?
example.correct_answer: Because she saw the angel and was protecting Balaam

misconceptions.cause: Balaam's own words in the story make the donkey sound stubborn.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Because she was stubborn" beside "Because she saw the angel and was protecting Balaam" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Numbers 22:33 where the angel explains.
misconceptions.feedback: The donkey turned aside because she saw the angel. The angel said that if she had not, he would have killed Balaam (Numbers 22:33).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 41:16: "I cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh the answer".

misconceptions.feedback: The seven fat cows and seven good ears stood for seven years of plenty. The seven thin cows stood for seven years of famine.

misconceptions.help: Draw it: fat cows are plenty, thin cows are famine.

misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the fear of the Lord means being terrified of God.

misconceptions.cause: The word fear means fright in daily speech.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "To be scared of God and hide from him" beside "To honour God and obey him" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Compare with respecting a good teacher or a loving parent.
misconceptions.feedback: The fear of the Lord means honouring God and obeying him because we love him. It is the beginning of wisdom (Proverbs 1:7).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks wisdom comes only from school or from age.

example.question: Where does true wisdom begin, according to Proverbs 1:7?
example.wrong_answer: With being old and having many degrees
example.correct_answer: With honouring the Lord

misconceptions.cause: The child links wisdom with grown-ups and school.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "With being old and having many degrees" beside "With honouring the Lord" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Remind the child that Joseph was a young man in prison.
misconceptions.feedback: Proverbs 1:7 says the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Joseph was young and in prison, yet God gave him wisdom.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks that a wise person should take the praise for himself.

example.question: Joseph was praised by Pharaoh. What did Joseph first say?
example.correct_answer: That God gives the answer

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "That he alone was wise" beside "That God gives the answer" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 41:16 and ask who got the credit.
misconceptions.feedback: Joseph gave the credit to God (Genesis 41:16). A wise person depends on God and gives him the praise.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.help: Make two columns: Nain and Jairus.

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "He was afraid of his master" beside "It would be a sin against God" and ask the child to choose.

misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks that trusting God means doing nothing ourselves.

example.question: Wanjiru trusts God to help her in an exam. What fits?

example.correct_answer: She studies and prays
